exampleAnswers.title: Expressing a Compound Predicate in Symbolic Form

question.text:
$x$ is even or odd.

Express the compound predicate above in symbolic form given the following notations:

  • $P(x):$ $x$ is even

  • $Q(x):$ $x$ is odd
question.explanation:
The word "or" is represented by the symbol "$\lor$".

So, the sentence reads

\[ \underbrace{x \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is even} }_{P} \quad \underbrace{\vphantom{p}\textbf{or}}_{\lor} \quad \underbrace{x \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is odd} }_{Q}, \]

that is, $P \lor Q.$

Express the compound predicate above in symbolic form given the following notations:

  • $P(x):$ $x$ is a multiple of $3$

\[ \underbrace{x \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is a multiple of $3$} }_P \quad \underbrace{\vphantom{p}\textrm{and}}_{\land} \quad \underbrace{x \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is a multiple of $5$} }_Q, \]

that is, $P \land Q.$

exampleAnswers.title: Expressing a Nested Compound Predicate in Symbolic Form

question.text:
$x$ is odd or even, and $x$ is negative or positive.

Express the compound predicate above in symbolic form given the following notations:

  • $O(x):$ $x$ is odd

  • $E(x):$ $x$ is even

  • $N(y):$ $y$ is negative

  • $P(y):$ $y$ is positive
question.explanation:
The word "and" is represented by the symbol "$\land$," while the word "or" is represented by the symbol "$\lor.$"

Note that this sentence consists of two parts:

  • Part 1: $x$ is odd or even. This corresponds to \[ \underbrace{x \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is odd } }_{O} \quad \underbrace{\vphantom{p}\textbf{or}}_{\lor} \quad \underbrace{x \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is even } }_{E}, \] that is, $O \lor E.$

  • Part 2: $y$ is negative or positive. This corresponds to \[ \underbrace{y \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is negative } }_{N} \quad \underbrace{\vphantom{p}\textbf{or}}_{\lor} \quad \underbrace{y \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is positive } }_{P}, \] that is, $N \lor P.$

So, we can express the sentence as \[ \underbrace{x \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is odd or even} }_{O \, \lor \, E} \quad \underbrace{\vphantom{p}\textbf{and}}_{\land} \quad \underbrace{x \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is negative or positive } }_{N \, \lor \, P}, \]

that is, $(O \lor E) \land (N \lor P).$

example.title: Expressing a Nested Compound Predicate in Symbolic Form

question.text:
$x$ is negative or an integer, or $x$ is greater than $4.$

Express the compound predicate above in symbolic form given the following notations:

  • $N(x):$ $x$ is negative

  • $I(x):$ $x$ is an integer

  • $G(x):$ $x$ is greater than $4$
question.explanation:
The word "or" is represented by the symbol "$\lor.$"

Note that this sentence consists of two parts:

  • Part 1: $x$ is negative or an integer. This corresponds to \[ \underbrace{x \,\textrm{is negative} }_N \quad \underbrace{\vphantom{p}\textrm{or}}_{\lor} \quad \underbrace{x \,\textrm{is an integer }}_I, \] that is, $N \lor I.$

  • Part 2: $x$ is greater than $4.$ This corresponds to $G.$

So, we can express the sentence as \[ \underbrace{x \,\textrm{is negative or an integer }}_{N \lor I} \quad \underbrace{\vphantom{p}\textrm{or}}_{\lor} \quad \underbrace{x \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is greater than }4 }_{G}, \]

that is, $N \lor I \lor G.$

example.title: Expressing a Nested Compound Predicate in Symbolic Form

question.text:
$x$ is a prime and less than $15$, and $x$ is odd.

Express the compound predicate above in symbolic form given the following notations:

  • $P(x):$ $x$ is prime

  • $L(x):$ $x$ is less than $15$

  • $O(x):$ $x$ is odd
question.explanation:
The word "and" is represented by the symbol "$\land.$"

Note that this sentence consists of two parts:

  • Part 1: $x$ is a prime and less than $15.$ This corresponds to \[ \underbrace{x \,\textrm{is prime} }_P \quad \underbrace{\vphantom{p}\textrm{and}}_{\land} \quad \underbrace{x \,\textrm{is less than }15}_L, \] that is, $P \land L.$

  • Part 2: $x$ is odd. This corresponds to $O.$

So, we can express the sentence as \[ \underbrace{x \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is a prime and less than }15 }_{P\land L} \quad \underbrace{\vphantom{p}\textrm{and}}_{\land} \quad \underbrace{x \,\textrm{is odd }}_{O}, \]

that is, $P \land L \land O.$

example.title: Expressing a Nested Compound Predicate in Symbolic Form

question.text:
$x$ is greater than $10$ and prime, or $x$ is negative.

Express the compound predicate above in symbolic form given the following notations:

  • $F(x):$ $x$ is greater than $10$

  • $G(x):$ $x$ is prime

  • $H(x):$ $x$ is negative
question.explanation:
The word "and" is represented by the symbol "$\land,$" while the word "or" is represented by the symbol "$\lor.$"

Note that this sentence consists of two parts:

  • Part 1: $x$ is greater than $10$ and prime. This corresponds to \[ \underbrace{x \,\textrm{is greater than} \,10 }_F \quad \underbrace{\vphantom{p}\textrm{and}}_{\land} \quad \underbrace{x \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is prime} }_G, \] that is, $F \land G.$

  • Part 2: $x$ is negative. This corresponds to $H.$

So, we can express the sentence as \[ \underbrace{x \,\textrm{ is greater than}\, 10\,\textrm{and prime} }_{F \land G} \quad \underbrace{\vphantom{p}\textrm{or}}_{\lor} \quad \underbrace{x \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is negative} }_H, \] that is, $(F \land G) \lor H.$

example.title: Expressing a Nested Compound Predicate in Symbolic Form

question.text:
$x$ is negative and irrational, or $x$ is positive and less than $5.$

Express the compound predicate above in symbolic form given the following notations:

  • $N(x):$ $x$ is negative

  • $W(x):$ $x$ is irrational

  • $P(x):$ $x$ is positive

  • $U(x):$ $x$ is less than $5$
question.explanation:
The word "and" is represented by the symbol "$\land,$" while the word "or" is represented by the symbol "$\lor.$"

Note that this sentence consists of two parts:

  • Part 1: $x$ is negative and irrational. This corresponds to \[ \underbrace{x \,\textrm{is negative} }_N \quad \underbrace{\vphantom{p}\textrm{and}}_{\land} \quad \underbrace{x \,\textrm{is irrational} }_W, \] that is, $N \land W.$

  • Part 2: $x$ is positive and less than $5.$ This corresponds to \[ \underbrace{x \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is positive } }_P \quad \underbrace{\vphantom{p}\textrm{and}}_{\land} \quad \underbrace{x \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is less than }5 }_U, \] that is, $P \land U.$

So, we can express the sentence as \[ \underbrace{x \,\textrm{is negative and irrational} }_{N \land W} \quad \underbrace{\vphantom{p}\textrm{or}}_{\lor} \quad \underbrace{x \vphantom{p}\textrm{ is positive and less than }5 }_{P \land U}, \]

that is, $(N \land W) \lor (P \land U).$

question.text: The shaded regions above represent the truth sets of the predicates $P(x,y)$ and $Q(x,y),$ defined over the universal set $\mathbb{R}^2.$ Which of the following is the truth set of $P \land Q?$
question.explanation:
The truth set of $P(x,y) \land Q(x,y)$ represents the intersection of the truth sets of $P(x,y)$ and $Q(x,y){:}$

\[ T_{P \land Q} = T_P \cap T_Q \]

Therefore, to get the truth set of $P(x,y) \land Q(x,y),$ we take all the points that belong to both $T_P$ and $T_Q,$ as shown below.

Note: The point where the dashed line meets the solid line does not belong to $T_P \cap T_Q$, since this point is not in $T_Q.$

example.title: Finding Truth Sets of Conjunctions and Disjunctions

question.text:
Find the truth set of $P(x) \lor Q(x)$ given the following predicates defined over the set of all positive integers:

  • $P(x):$ $6$ is divisible by $x$

  • $Q(x):$ $10$ is divisible by $x$
question.explanation:
The truth set of $P(x) \lor Q(x)$ represents the union of the truth sets of $P(x)$ and $Q(x){:}$ \[ T_{P \lor Q} = T_P \cup T_Q \]

We start by finding the truth sets of $P(x)$ and $Q(x){:}$

  • The truth set of $P(x)$ is \[ T_P = \big\{ 1,2,3,6 \big\}. \]

  • The truth set of $Q(x)$ is \[ T_Q = \big\{ 1,2,5,10 \big\}. \]

Therefore, we have \begin{align*} T_{P \lor Q} &= T_P \cup T_Q \\[3pt] &= \big\{ 1,2,3,6 \big\} \cup \big\{1,2,5,10 \big\} \\[3pt] &= \big\{ 1,2,3,5,6,10 \big\}. \end{align*}

example.title: Finding Truth Sets of Conjunctions and Disjunctions

question.text:
Find the truth set of $P(x) \lor Q(x)$ given the following predicates defined over the set of all positive integers:

  • $P(x):$ $x$ divides $10$

  • $Q(x):$ $x$ is less than $6$
question.explanation:
The truth set of $P(x) \lor Q(x)$ represents the union of the truth sets of $P(x)$ and $Q(x){:}$ \[ T_{P \lor Q} = T_P \cup T_Q \]

We start by finding the truth sets of $P(x)$ and $Q(x){:}$

  • The truth set of $P(x)$ is \[ T_P = \big\{ 1, 2, 5, 10 \big\}. \]

  • The truth set of $Q(x)$ is \[ T_Q = \big\{ 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 \big\}. \]

Therefore, we have \begin{align*} T_{P \lor Q} &= T_P \cup T_Q \\[3pt] &=\big\{ 1,2,5,10 \big\} \cup \big\{ 1,2,3,4,5 \big\} \\[3pt] &= \big\{ 1,2,3,4, 5,10 \big\}. \end{align*}

question.text:
Find the truth set of $P(x) \lor Q(x)$ given the following predicates defined over the set of all positive integers:

  • $P(x):$ $x$ divides $9$

  • $Q(x):$ $x$ is less than $1$
question.explanation:
The truth set of $P(x) \lor Q(x)$ represents the union of the truth sets of $P(x)$ and $Q(x){:}$ \[ T_{P \lor Q} = T_P \cup T_Q \]

We start by finding the truth sets of $P(x)$ and $Q(x){:}$

  • The truth set of $P(x)$ is \[ T_P = \big\{ 1, 3, 9 \big\}. \]

  • The truth set of $Q(x)$ is \[ T_Q = \emptyset, \] the empty set, since there are no positive integers $x$ less than $1.$

Therefore, we have \begin{align*} T_{P \lor Q} &= T_P \cup T_Q \\[3pt] &=\big\{ 1,3,9 \big\} \cup \emptyset \\[3pt] &= \big\{ 1,3,9 \big\}. \end{align*}

exampleAnswers.title: Using Laws Involving Conjunction and Disjunction

question.text: Simplify the sentence "$x$ is positive, or it is positive or rational."
question.explanation:
First, let's rewrite the phrase "it is positive or rational" as the equivalent phrase "it is positive or it is rational." The sentence now reads

"$x$ is positive, or it is positive or it is rational."

Then, using the associative law, we can move the comma:

"$x$ is positive or it is positive, or it is rational."

Now, we can simplify the phrase "$x$ is positive or it is positive" to just "$x$ is positive." The sentence now reads

"$x$ is positive, or it is rational."

Finally, we can write the sentence more concisely as

"$x$ is positive or rational."

"$n$ is a multiple of $2,$ and it is a multiple of $2$ and it is a multiple of $5.$"

"$n$ is a multiple of $2$ and it is a multiple of $2,$ and it is a multiple of $5.$"

Now, we can simplify the phrase "$n$ is a multiple of $2$ and it is a multiple of $2$" to just "$n$ is a multiple of $2.$" The sentence now reads

Finally, we can write the sentence more concisely as
